diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Although Theorem~\ref{thm:dimfree_lip_velocity} is stated and proved in finite dimensions in \cite{meng2025pathway},
its Lipschitz bound involves constants that are independent of the ambient dimension.
We therefore interpret it as a function-space stability statement.

We work in a function-space regime: let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable Hilbert space with norm
$\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{H}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is stated on a separable Hilbert space (Assumption assu:gaussian_tail_function_space is infinite-dimensional), but the only justification is a citation whose proof is finite-dimensional, plus the remark's inference that dimension-free constants suffice. Dimension-free constants alone do not imply the infinite-dimensional statement: existence of the Föllmer process in infinite dimensions and convergence of finite-dimensional approximations (preserving the Lipschitz bound) require a nontrivial argument that is not given. The remark concedes the gap ('we therefore interpret it as...'), so the theorem is unsupported as written in the function-space regime.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either supply the missing infinite-dimensional argument (e.g., Galerkin/projection approximation with convergence of the Föllmer drifts under the trace-class and uniform Fréchet bounds of Assumption assu:gaussian_tail_function_space), or restate the theorem as a finite-dimensional result with dimension-free constants and explicitly demote the function-space version to a heuristic.
issues.overall_effect: The entire function-space Lipschitz-transport chain (Theorem thm:dimfree_lip_velocity -> lem:avg_velocity_lipschitz -> cor:exists_lipschitz_onestep, and the informal main-text Theorem thm:lipschitz_onestep_main) is established only in finite dimensions with dimension-free constants; the abstract/Section sec:lipschitz_colored claim of Lipschitz regularity 'in the function-space limit' rests on an unproved extension.
issues.title: Function-space Föllmer-velocity Lipschitz theorem asserted on a Hilbert space but supported only by a finite-dimensional citation
issues.why_classification: A contained nontrivial approximation argument under the stated strong assumptions plausibly closes the gap, and the fallback (finite-dimensional theorem with dimension-free constants) is a limited weakening that preserves the paper's dimension-robustness message; no global proof architecture is lost, but the formal function-space statement cannot stand as cited.

issues.failure_explanation: By eq:avg_velocity_def, w(z;r,t) averages v along the trajectory of v with terminal point z, so differentiating in z brings in the Jacobian of the ODE flow map z_t -> z_tau, whose norm is bounded by a Grönwall factor exp(int_tau^t Lip(v(s,.))ds), not by 1. The asserted first inequality drops this factor and no proof is given. It is false in general: the linear contractive field v(x,t) = -L_0 t x satisfies Lip(v(t,.)) <= L_0 t, yet the backward flow gives z_tau = e^{L_0(t^2-tau^2)/2} z_t, hence w(z;0,1) = -(e^{L_0/2}-1) z and the one-step map T(xi) = xi - w(xi;0,1) = e^{L_0/2} xi has Lip(T) = e^{L_0/2} > 1 + L_0/2 for every L_0 > 0. Such contractive linear velocities are exactly those arising when transporting a Gaussian to a more concentrated Gaussian target (the generic posterior-versus-prior situation), so the failure is not pathological. The corollary's bound (1 + L_0/2) inherits the error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the averaging inequality by the Grönwall bound Lip(w(.;r,t)) <= (1/(t-r)) int_r^t Lip(v(tau,.)) exp(int_tau^t Lip(v(s,.))ds) dtau, and restate the corollary and Theorem thm:lipschitz_onestep_main with the corrected constant Lip(T) <= exp(L_0/2).
issues.overall_effect: The explicit dimension-free bounds Lip(w(.;0,1)) <= L_0/2 and Lip(T) <= 1 + L_0/2 in lem:avg_velocity_lipschitz, cor:exists_lipschitz_onestep and the informal Theorem thm:lipschitz_onestep_main are unsupported and false in general; only the qualitative claim (a globally Lipschitz one-step map with a dimension-free constant) survives, with a larger constant such as exp(L_0/2).
issues.title: Averaged-velocity Lipschitz bound omits the ODE flow-map Jacobian and is false in general, invalidating the 1 + L_0/2 one-step bound
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard but nontrivial flow-map/Grönwall argument and the advertised quantitative constant must be weakened (a genuine loss relative to the stated bound); however the qualitative dimension-free Lipschitz conclusion, which is what the paper's narrative uses, survives, so no new global architecture or major loss results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: compared with multistep diffusion, our one-step generative transport yields faster sampling and more accurate posterior summaries under the observation setting considered.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts that the multistep diffusion baseline consistently underperforms the one-step Mean Flows model in posterior statistics (echoed in the main text as 'more accurate posterior summaries'). The paper's own tables refute the universal claim: for Advection with the anisotropic reference, the diffusion model attains posterior-std error epsilon_sigma^eval = 4.30e-2 (tab:diffusion), which is better than the one-step model's 5.09e-2 (tab:benchmark_summary). The one-step model is uniformly much faster and more accurate in the remaining cells, but 'consistently underperforms ... in posterior statistics' is false as stated.

failure_location.quote: the multistep baseline consistently underperforms our one-step model in posterior statistics, while incurring a much higher sampling cost.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword both passages to a qualified claim, e.g., the one-step model is dramatically faster and achieves comparable or better posterior statistics in all but one reported case (Advection epsilon_sigma^eval); no change to any experiment, table, or formal result is needed.
issues.overall_effect: A comparative-performance claim about the paper's central one-step-vs-multistep paradigm comparison is overstated; readers are told accuracy dominance is uniform when the reported data show one counterexample (Advection posterior standard deviation).
issues.title: Universal claim that the multistep diffusion baseline 'consistently underperforms' the one-step model is contradicted by the paper's own tables
issues.why_classification: A short local rewording fully fixes the defect while preserving every substantive claim (speed advantage and overall accuracy trend); no mathematical content, method, or guarantee is affected.
